Scales decoded tangent slopes, then normalizes and smoothly limits tilt. It does not scale XY before reconstructing Z. Zero gives an unperturbed liquid surface over the substrate main normal.

Master strength for the entire liquid layer: coverage, pigment, normals and interface response. Zero leaves the dry material. Under wet coverage the liquid replaces the common Clearcoat interface, never stacks a second coat.

Fine normal influence on liquid pigment lighting only. Default zero. Never perturbs the substrate diffuse or its hard Toon shadow; wet reflections always use the liquid surface normal.
Artistic gain for the single liquid GGX direct/probe lobe. Zero hides reflected light, but does not disable pigment or interface transmission. Use Layer Strength to disable the entire layer.
Shader.Category: Unified coverage, independent pigment, stable normals and a single dielectric wet interface. LiquidX overlays already rendered surfaces; no GrabPass or volumetric water.
Shader.Property: 0 Raw AG; 1 Exported AG PNG (encoded RGB, numerical alpha; import as data); 2 Unity Normal. Explicit formats, not automatic detection. Never combine mode 1 with automatic sRGB decode. Keep game runtime sampling flags for mode 0.

Custom coverage in R, linear data. Used in Custom Mask mode. LiquidTiling then its own ST, repeat/trilinear/aniso8 sampling. Zero means no liquid.
Rejects low pattern/custom-mask values, then remaps the remainder. Does not clip the mesh or use Liquid Color A. Zero-coverage pixels are unchanged.
Smooth transition above the cutoff, augmented by pixel derivatives. Applied before KKS stage amounts so region animation remains continuous.
Smooth bound on decoded detail tilt in degrees, relative to the substrate main normal. Limits steep grazing ridges without changing roughness to hide decode errors.
Normal-variance specular anti-aliasing. Broadens unresolved high-frequency reflections. Zero disables variance broadening, not texture mip filtering.
Liquid interface refractive index, independent of common Clearcoat. 1.33 gives approximately 0.02 normal-incidence reflectance. 1 disables interface reflection. This is not screen-space refraction.
Independent gain for liquid reflection probes. Does not require the dry Reflection Mode or dry Reflection Mask. Base pass only; not duplicated by additional lights.
Mixes pigment soft lighting toward the substrate Toon visibility. Does not quantize liquid GGX or alter transparent-film substrate lighting.
0 final; 1 effective coverage; 2 coverage-masked world normal; 3 liquid direct specular; 4 liquid environment; 5 pigment opacity; 6 raw coverage before cleanup.

Substrate attenuation strength, default 0.25. 0 preserves the underlying lighting; 1 applies full approximate interface transmission and substrate index matching. Does not change liquid direct/probe highlights. Independent of pigment alpha. Low values are an artistic energy override. LiquidX applies the same view attenuation to framebuffer blending.

Liquid detail influence on the transmission normal, default 0. Zero uses the substrate main normal to prevent droplet slopes carving dark grooves into the underlying material. One uses full liquid detail. Reflections always retain full liquid normals. This is separate from LiquidDiffuseNormal for pigment shading.

Optional pigment shadow tint: RGB is a bounded multiplicative tint, A is its strength (default 0). Fades with Liquid Color A and Color Strength. Never tints a clear film, wet highlights or the dry substrate. Does not fill missing light, disable cast shadows, or control Fresnel attenuation; use LiquidEnergyBlend for that.

Main normal-map influence on direct Toon diffuse only. 0 uses the mesh normal for this input; detail remains independently adjustable. Does not reduce specular, environment, Clearcoat or liquid normals. Default 1. UseRamp=0 retains continuous lighting.

Detail normal-map influence on direct Toon diffuse only. Independent of ToonNormalInfluence; default 1. Specular, environment and Clearcoat keep full normals. SkinX uses its existing SkinDiffuseNormalDetail instead.

Pixel-derivative filtering strength for procedural Toon bands and the diffuse geometric horizon. Default 1; 0 disables this extra AA, not texture filtering. Does not blur textures or remove large normal/compression blocks. Texture ramps retain their own sampler filtering.

Renamed from ToonDarkFillColor; the optional colored-fill calculation is unchanged. RGB multiplies albedo; A is strength, default 0, not coverage. Still respects physical cast shadows. Use ToonMinLighting, not this color, to lift self-shadowed areas. Base-only, main-light-driven, off with UseRamp=0. Old game-card values under ToonDarkFillColor must be reapplied to this new property; no runtime migration plugin is included.

Minimum normalized main-light Toon diffuse response after the diffuse horizon and cast shadows: u becomes m+(1-m)*u. Default 0.15 provides a gentle shadow lift. Set 0 to disable; explicitly saved material values are preserved. Lifts both self and external shadows, not final RGB or GI; albedo, main light intensity/color, distance/cookie and material layer attenuation still apply. Base-only, no repeated Add lift, disabled with UseRamp=0. Does not change specular/coat/reflection lobes. Set ToonShadeColor A=0 when tuning this control alone.

Transition hue, luminance-normalized before blending. Independent of albedo and coat color.

Lifts both self and external shadows, not final RGB or GI; albedo, main light intensity/color, distance/cookie and material layer attenuation still apply. Base-only, no repeated Add lift, disabled with UseRamp=0. Does not change specular/coat/reflection lobes. Set ToonShadeColor A=0 when tuning this control alone.
